cells.tense: The pen is in your hand now, and what you picture has been earned.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Step toward what you've been picturing — one step, this year's version of you, not a plan. Make it small enough that no one would call it a beginning. It still counts the way a first step counts, and nobody has to bless it first.
cells.core:
You can walk without seeing the end of it. Enough light for the next step arrives when you need it, and you've learned to take that step rather than wait for the way to explain itself. What you picture now stands on things you've finished, because you let the old ones close cleanly.

So when a want shows up, back it with weight today. Moving from what you actually feel, in a direction you'd still choose tomorrow, keeps the dreaming useful instead of decorative. Letting go cleared the space; this is what the space is for. A single step keeps the whole thing honest, and it doesn't need permission, including from a better version of you.
cells.sheetLine: You dream from what you've completed, and one step is enough.
cells.verb: Moving when you can't see the whole road
cells.place: Where it's safe to let things end

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead a future is being imagined that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: give it what it needs today, not what it is scheduled for
cells.ask: Choose what you're dreaming about and give it what it actually needs today, not what the calendar says. If the plan slips a week, it slips. Care that runs at the pace of the thing survives; care that runs on your schedule burns you down.
cells.core:
What you picture has been running ahead of what is really there. The dream gets taken for the ground under you, and you plan against a version that hasn't happened, so the hours you have go to managing a scene hardly anyone else can see. That's tiring, and the tiredness isn't proof you care most.

Feed what is actually growing. Care that waits for its own pace, and lets a thing be small without grading it, gets further than care that pushes. Letting go happens by itself once you stop holding the schedule tighter than the thing. What you want is still there — it just grows slower than the plan says, and it grew fine before the plan existed.
cells.sheetLine: You're caretaking a future that hasn't arrived, and it's tiring.
cells.verb: Moving when you can't see the whole road
cells.place: Where it's safe to let things end

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Hold off on the list until the piece that matters makes itself known — then start there and leave the rest where they sit. Don't sort it into a scheme. Begin with what's asking to be begun, and let the others keep waiting.
cells.core:
You take what's here as all there is, and the quieter perceptions you have go unattended because nothing has proven them. The doorstep is behind you now, and your feet haven't said so. There's a plainness in this that works — much of what people say is decoration — and it costs you what shows up before thinking does.

So don't chase the big framework; don't rehearse a statement of trust. Start with one suspicion and hold it a day before you decide about it. What lands with no argument underneath is the patch you step onto, and other patches will show after that.
cells.sheetLine: You gave up on knowing things before you can prove them.

cells.tense: You move through your days as if someone else wrote the plan.
cells.act: do the plain version first, before the plans
cells.ask: Do the plain form of a thing today — no plan around it, nothing to show at the end. If it feels pointless, it still counts. This is where your own hand starts being visible in the making.
cells.core:
There's a picture of where your life is heading, and you talk about it as though it formed somewhere else and simply applies to you. Days pass and you notice what got made of them, not what you kept making by choosing. The picture isn't a stranger's — you drew it, and you don't recognize the hand. A lot of people near you may not either, which is why nobody has said anything.

So do one small unglamorous thing today, before the master plan, alone. A set of ten minutes, repeated, where nobody watches. You saw yourself repeating it long before you called it a vision, which is the part being forgotten while you discuss the vision instead of doing it.
cells.sheetLine: You talk about your direction like it wasn't yours to write.
